items.followUp: Define a coordinate covalent bond and explain its formation in the hydronium ion, H₃O⁺.

rubric.why: Checks the defining feature of a coordinate covalent bond.
rubric.description: Both electrons in the shared pair are donated by one atom.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that one atom provides both electrons in the shared pair.

rubric.why: Checks the species involved in the ammonia example.
rubric.description: Nitrogen in NH₃ donates a lone pair to H⁺.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying NH₃ and H⁺ as the reactants.

rubric.why: Checks the donation and product in the ammonia example.
rubric.description: Nitrogen donates its lone pair to form NH₄⁺.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying the lone-pair donation and formation of NH₄⁺.

rubric.why: Checks the species involved in the water example.
rubric.description: Oxygen in H₂O donates a lone pair to H⁺.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying H₂O and H⁺ as the reactants.

rubric.why: Checks the donation and product in the water example.
rubric.description: Oxygen donates its lone pair to form H₃O⁺.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying the lone-pair donation and formation of H₃O⁺.

modelAnswer: A coordinate covalent bond is a covalent bond in which both shared electrons are donated by one atom.
In NH₃, nitrogen donates a lone pair to H⁺, forming NH₄⁺; the N→H bond is coordinate covalent.
In H₂O, oxygen donates a lone pair to H⁺, forming H₃O⁺; the O→H bond is coordinate covalent.

items.followUp: Define solubility and state two factors that affect the solubility of gases in liquids.

rubric.why: Checks the definition and the condition under which solubility is specified.
rubric.description: Solubility is the maximum amount of solute that dissolves in a given amount of solvent at a specified temperature.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the maximum amount of solute dissolving in a given amount of solvent at a specified temperature.

rubric.why: Checks the principle relating the nature of the solute and solvent.
rubric.description: Like dissolves like: polar substances dissolve in polar solvents, and nonpolar substances dissolve in nonpolar solvents.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating the principle or correctly matching polar and nonpolar substances with their solvents.

rubric.why: Checks the general effect of temperature on the solubility of solid solutes.
rubric.description: The solubility of most solids in liquids increases as temperature increases.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that the solubility of most solids increases with temperature.

rubric.why: Checks the effect of pressure on the solubility of gases in liquids.
rubric.description: The solubility of gases in liquids increases as pressure increases.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that increasing pressure increases gas solubility.

modelAnswer: Solubility is the maximum amount of a solute that dissolves in a given amount of solvent at a specified temperature.
Like dissolves like: polar substances dissolve in polar solvents, and nonpolar substances dissolve in nonpolar solvents.
The solubility of most solids in liquids increases as temperature increases.
The solubility of gases in liquids decreases as temperature increases and increases as pressure increases.

items.followUp: State two properties of a proton.

rubric.why: Checks the electrical property of a neutron.
rubric.description: A neutron has no electrical charge.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that a neutron is neutral or has zero charge.

rubric.why: Checks another characteristic property of a neutron.
rubric.description: A neutron has a mass of approximately 1 amu and is present in the nucleus.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating its approximate mass or its location in the nucleus.

modelAnswer: A neutron has no electrical charge.
A neutron has a mass of approximately 1 amu and is present in the nucleus of an atom.

items.followUp: Define atomic radius and give the atomic radius of hydrogen as an example.

rubric.why: Checks the definition of atomic radius.
rubric.description: Atomic radius is the distance from the nucleus to the outermost electron shell of an atom.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for giving the distance from the nucleus to the outermost electron shell.

rubric.why: Checks that a valid example of atomic radius is given.
rubric.description: For example, the atomic radius of sodium is approximately 186 pm.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for naming sodium and giving its approximate atomic radius as 186 pm.

modelAnswer: Atomic radius is the distance from the nucleus of an atom to its outermost electron shell.
For example, the atomic radius of sodium is approximately 186 pm.
